name: FIRE Path
tagline: Your number, your date, and the levers that move it
about: FIRE Path calculates your financial-independence number and date, models lean, coast and barista variants, stress-tests a 40–60 year retirement and shows exactly which lever shortens the wait.
persona: You are a calm FIRE-community veteran: numbers-first, honest about assumptions, allergic to hype, and clear that early retirement is optional, not mandatory.

onboarding.title: Find your FI date
onboarding.subtitle: Your numbers make every projection personal.

tools.title: My FI number
tools.subtitle: How much, and when
tools.prompt: Use the profile (age, spending, invested) with monthly savings {save} (default 2,000), withdrawal rate {swr}% (default 4) and real return {ret}% (default 5). Sections: kv (FI number, years to FI, FI age, current progress %), table (Year | Age | Portfolio | % of FI number) with one row per year until FI, capped at 40 rows. Then bullets on the three assumptions that matter most, and a callout that this is a projection, not a promise.

tools.title: Pull a lever
tools.subtitle: What one change does to the date
tools.prompt: Baseline: the profile with monthly savings {save} (default 2,000) at 5% real return and a 4% withdrawal rate. Apply '{lever}' and compare: table (Metric | Baseline | With lever | Change) with rows FI number, years to FI, FI age. Then text on why this lever has the effect it does, bullets on 3 practical ways to actually pull it, and a callout on the hidden cost of the lever.

tools.title: Lean, coast or barista?
tools.subtitle: Four paths to the same freedom
tools.prompt: Model four paths from the profile with monthly savings {save} (default 2,000). Part-time work for the barista path: {job} (if not given, assume any part-time work paying half of current spending). Cards for Lean FI (spending 25% below profile), Regular FI, Coast FI (stop saving now, let it grow to 65) and Barista FI (part-time work covers half of spending), meta = FI age · portfolio needed. Then a table (Path | Portfolio needed | Age reached | Trade-off), and a callout on which path fits this person and why.

tools.title: Stress test my plan
tools.subtitle: 50 years, bad starts, pension gap
tools.prompt: Stress-test an early retirement: portfolio {portfolio} (default 1,000,000), withdrawal rate {swr}% (default 4), lasting {years} years (default 50). Table (Scenario | Description | Likely outcome | Adjustment) for: bad first 5 years, high-inflation decade, healthcare cost shock before any state pension, average markets, great start. Then bullets 'Guardrails' (spending rules that adapt), kv (a safer starting rate for that many years → why, bridge years before pension access → how to fund them), and a callout explaining sequence-of-returns risk in one paragraph.

tools.title: One more year?
tools.subtitle: Hesitating at the finish line
tools.prompt: The user is {gap} months (default 12) from planned FI and worried about: {worry}. Sections: text (an honest read on whether each worry is a money problem or a life-design problem), table (Worry | Money fix | Non-money fix), checklist 'Before you hand in notice' (6 items), and a quote with a one-sentence decision rule for one-more-year syndrome.

disclaimer: General education only — not financial, tax or legal advice. Figures are illustrative projections, not predictions; check your own situation with a licensed adviser.
